frontier.hypothesis: Route (A) is not yet fully searched: a SECOND, BYTE-PRODUCING use of the +0x44C address INSIDE the qf&0x30 block would keep the address pseudo's reference count non-zero while the same cse table is still live, which is the only way to close region A that is not dead-in-output codegen steering.
frontier.mechanism: delete_dead_from_cse deletes an address SET only when its destination pseudo's whole-function reference count is zero (cse.c:8730-8734); a use inside the block keeps the count non-zero AND keeps the expression in the same cse basic block's hash table, so find_best_addr's ADDRESS_COST comparison (cse.c:2698-2739) restores register+displacement at all three sites. K14 showed a use in a LATER cse block does not work.
frontier.next_probe: Re-read asm/funcs/func_8003B9D0.s 0x8003BAAC-0x8003BAEC asking only one question: does any instruction target actually emits in that window consume the +0x44C ADDRESS as a value? In particular check the jal func_8003AFFC argument setup (m2c infers func_8003AFFC(D_800A3878), so $a0 is the OTHER object -- but confirm no second argument register is set from $s0+0x44C) and the two 0x32 stores. If nothing there consumes the address as a value, route (A) is empty of honest forms and the function's whole remaining problem is route (B)'s placements.

frontier.hypothesis: If route (A) is empty, the cheapest LEGAL closure of region A remains session-3's if/ELSE diamond (measured 11, build_insns 185 == target 185, target's exact region-A bytes), and the entire remaining work is buying back its two placement clusters.
frontier.mechanism: An if/ELSE arm ends in an unconditional jump + BARRIER, so cse_end_of_basic_block (cse.c:8039-8184) cannot AROUND-extend past the join label and eda enters the next block with no qty_const -- the fold cannot fire regardless of the hash table. The price is that magic = 0x80190800 sinks out of the prologue into the else arm (~7) and the la moves from inside the qf&0x30 block to mine[38..39] (~4).
frontier.next_probe: Note first that magic's placement is a FRONT-END consequence of the if/else (target's tgt[1..3] lui/ori in the prologue proves the original used a plain if there), so it cannot be bought back while the boundary comes from THAT if. The probe is therefore to find a different statement between the pointer's assignment and the qf&0x30 block that can honestly carry a two-arm shape -- and, per session-4 K11, without introducing a multi-use join label, since all 13 labels in target appear exactly twice.
